meta.purpose: US-only gas lengths held in km go back to the miles their sources state

verifications.note: Chandeleur System: ~215 miles of offshore Mississippi

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 215.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 215 mi. The EnLink 2014 press release says the Chandeleur system is about 215 miles. The sheet holds 215 labeled km, which would be 133.6 miles. The number matches the source in miles, so the sheet unit looks wrong and the length should be 215 mi, not a conversion.

verifications.note: The Horizon Project will consist of 71 miles of high pressure pipeline

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 117.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 71 mi. Sources disagree. The 2000 filing says 71 miles in total, made of 28.5 miles of new pipe and about 42 miles leased. Natural Gas Intelligence says 74 miles. A 2001 Oil and Gas Journal item gives 27 new and 46 leased, which adds to 73. The sheet 117 km is 72.7 miles, between these. No source gives exactly 72.7, so the figure needs a person to choose. The 71 mile figure comes from the company's own filing, so it is used.

verifications.note: Tejas Gas is an approximately 3,400-mile natural gas

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 5221.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 3400 mi. The 2001 filing calls Tejas Gas an approximately 3,400-mile system. The sheet 5,221 km is 3,244 miles. The only source I found with 3,244 miles is a banned aggregator, so it is not cited. Later Kinder Morgan filings give only a combined Texas system of about 6,000 miles. The 3,400 figure is old and covers the company, so it is weak.

verifications.note: Project: Greater Philadelphia Expansion Project ... Length: 35 miles

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 56.30 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 35 mi. Pipeline News lists the project at 35 miles in October 2018. The sheet 56.3 km is 35.0 miles, so the sheet value is a conversion.

The sheet held 6.40 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 4 mi. The FERC assessment says about 4 miles of new 36-inch pipe, written as 4.0 mile in one place. The sheet 6.4 km is 3.98 miles. The EIA August 2026 release also lists 4 miles. The operator page mentions a separate 3.9-mile piece in Coden, Alabama.

verifications.note: a total of 4.8 miles of branch line loop extensions

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 5.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 5 mi. EIA lists the project at 5 miles. The FERC order says 4.8 miles of loop extensions. The sheet 5.0 km would be 3.1 miles, so the 5.0 looks like miles with the wrong unit. The number matches EIA in miles.

verifications.note: American Midstream (AlaTenn), LLC, which owns and operates approximately 295 miles of interstate pipeline that runs through the Tennessee River Valley from Selmer, Tennessee to Huntsville, Alabama

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 475.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 295 mi. American Midstream's 2012 annual report says the AlaTenn system is about 295 miles, which matches the sheet value of 475 km. The 2016 annual report and a Rextag listing say 294 miles. The difference is one mile.

verifications.note: With 1,526 miles (2,456 km) of pipeline, East Tennessee can deliver 1.86 Bcf/d

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 2456.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 1526 mi. Enbridge's July 2026 asset fact sheet gives East Tennessee Natural Gas as 1,526 miles, or 2,456 km. This is exactly the sheet value. A 2023 copy of the same fact sheet gives the same figure.

verifications.note: traveling a distance of 96 miles (154 km)

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 154.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 96 mi. The 2021 Enbridge fact sheet says 96 miles, or 154 km, which is the sheet value. The July 2026 fact sheet says 115 miles, or 185 km. Enbridge changed the figure between the two editions and does not say why. The newest figure is 115 miles. The current fact sheet says 115 miles. The older figure is kept because it matches the sheet. A person may want to move to 115. The archived copy read is from September 2021.

verifications.note: With 8,825 miles of pipeline, Texas Eastern Transmission

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 14202.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 8825 mi. The 2021 Enbridge fact sheet says 8,825 miles, which matches the sheet value of 14,202 km. The July 2026 fact sheet says 8,532 miles. Enbridge changed the system total between editions and does not say why. The newest figure is 8,532 miles. The current fact sheet says 8,532 miles. The older figure is kept because it matches the sheet. A person may want to move to 8,532. The archived copy read is from September 2021.

verifications.note: construct and operate a 23-mile-long, 48-inch-diameter, bi-directional pipeline from Corpus Christi Liquefaction's facilities to a point near the City of Sinton, Texas

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 37.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 23 mi. The 2014 FERC certificate order describes a 23-mile, 48-inch pipeline from the liquefaction plant to near Sinton, Texas. This matches the sheet value of 37 km. The order calls it the Cheniere Pipeline, which is the Corpus Christi Pipeline.

verifications.note: Phase II of the project included the construction of approximately 11 miles of pipeline looping

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 17.70 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 11 mi. The Williams press release from August 2020 says Phase II included about 11 miles of pipeline looping. This matches the sheet value of 17.7 km. The source says approximately 11, so the figure is rounded.

verifications.note: segments of 36-inch-diameter mainline loop extensions totaling 3.2 miles

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 5.10 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 3.2 mi. The February 2021 Federal Register notice says the application covers two segments of 36-inch mainline loop extensions totaling 3.2 miles in Calhoun and Jefferson Counties, Florida. This matches the sheet value of 5.1 km. The project is cancelled, so this is the planned length.

verifications.note: 517-mile Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) regulated interstate transmission pipeline system

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 732.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 517 mi. The owner's page says Eastern Shore has a 517-mile interstate pipeline system. The sheet 732 km is about 455 miles, which no source I opened states. Earlier owner press releases gave 442 miles in 2016 and 486 miles in 2019, so the system grew over time and 455 is not a figure I could place.

verifications.note: The Oasis Pipeline is a 600 mile, bi-directional pipeline that connects the Waha Hub to the Katy Hub

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 966.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 600 mi. The existing ref states 600 miles, which equals the sheet 966 km. The same deck also shows 583 miles on an earlier slide, so the 600 figure is the rounder one used in the text.

verifications.note: Transco owns and operates an approximately 9,600-mile natural gas pipeline system

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 10200.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 9600 mi. Williams says Transco is about 9,600 miles. The sheet 10,200 km is about 6,338 miles, so it is not a conversion of this figure. Transco's own 2023 annual report said about 9,700 miles of mainline and branch pipe, and a 2025 trade article said nearly 10,000 miles.

The sheet held 109.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 68 mi. The existing ref lists the Muskogee Pipeline at 68 miles, which equals the sheet 109 km. A December 2016 trade report gave 77 miles in search snippets, but I did not open it.

resolutions.segment_name: Regional Energy Access Project (Phase I and II)

verifications.note: Regional Energy Access Project (Phase I and II) ... Miles 35.8

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 54.70 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 35.8 mi. The newest EIA release gives 35.8 miles. The sheet 54.7 km is about 34.0 miles. News coverage of the federal environmental statement describes 22.2 miles plus 13.8 miles, which totals 36 miles, but I did not open that statement.
The sheet held 5.50 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 3.4 mi. The newest EIA release gives 3.4 miles for the Lamar County Expansion Project, which equals the sheet 5.5 km.

verifications.note: Florida Gas's transmission system consists of a 5,300-mile-long pipeline system
The Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) pipeline is an approximately 5,300-mile system

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 8529.52 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 5300 mi. A 2020 federal order and a 2020 Kinder Morgan page both call the whole system about 5,300 miles, which matches the sheet's 8,529.52 km. Newer material is higher. An Energy Transfer project document from June 2026 says about 5,400 miles, and Rextag says 5,380 miles. So 5,300 miles is the figure the older operator sources give, and newer sources round up to 5,400.

verifications.note: a small 367-mile pipeline owned by Black Bear Transmission

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 589.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 367 mi. Rextag says the pipeline is 367 miles, which is about 590.6 km. The sheet holds 589 km, which is 366 miles. They agree within rounding. The Black Bear page cited by the wiki loads but does not state a length in the page text I could read, so only Rextag is proposed.

verifications.note: Interstate pipeline table: Transwestern Pipeline, 100%, 2,590 miles of natural gas pipeline

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 4345.00 km, which is about 2,700 miles. Energy Transfer's annual report for 2024 lists Transwestern Pipeline at 2,590 miles, so the length becomes 2590 mi. That is the whole Transwestern system. No source gives the Main Line alone. Energy Transfer's 2011 report said about 2,690 miles and an April 2019 presentation said 2,570 miles, so the newest figure is used.

verifications.note: Project: TEMAX Project ... Length: 33 miles ... Clarington, OH - Delta, PA

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 53.10 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 33 mi. The journal lists the TEMAX Project at 33 miles from Clarington, Ohio to Delta, Pennsylvania. The sheet's 53.1 km is 33.0 miles. The 2013 Federal Register notice in the current refs describes about 33.6 miles of new 36-inch loop, but the verifier could not find the name TEMAX on it, so it is not used.

verifications.note: approximately 38 miles of pipeline looping facilities and other facility upgrades and modifications to DETI's existing system in Pennsylvania and West Virginia (Supply Header Project)

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 61.20 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 38 mi. The federal order describes the Supply Header Project as about 38 miles of pipeline looping. The sheet's 61.2 km is 38.0 miles. Other documents give 37.5 and 38.7 miles for earlier or later designs.

resolutions.segment_name: Rivervale South to Market Expansion Project
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 0.98 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 0.61 mi. The new pipe for the Rivervale South to Market project is a 0.61 mile loop in New Jersey. The sheet's 0.98 km is 0.61 miles. The project also uprates 10.35 miles of existing pipe, which is not new length and is not counted.

verifications.note: In addition to 2,200 miles of intrastate pipelines, EOIT has two underground natural gas storage facilities

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 3540.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 2200 mi. Enable's 2020 annual report says the Oklahoma intrastate system has 2,200 miles of pipeline. That is about 3,540 km, the same as the sheet. Enable's 2014 and 2018 reports said 2,300 miles, so the figure has moved over time.

verifications.note: The Garden Banks Pipeline is a 30-inch-diameter, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)-regulated offshore natural gas transmission pipeline, traveling a distance of 50 miles (80 km)

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 84.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 50 mi. Enbridge's fact sheet gives the Garden Banks Pipeline as 50 miles, or 80 km. The sheet holds 84 km, which is 52 miles. The same fact sheet gives 52 miles (84 km) for the separate Magnolia Gathering Pipeline in the same corridor, so the sheet figure may have come from that line. The fact sheet carries no date.

verifications.note: Sabine Pipe Line is a small 131-mile pipeline located between Erath, Louisiana, and Port Arthur, Texas

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 211.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 131 mi. The Rextag page gives the pipeline as 131 miles, about 211 km, the same as the sheet. EnLink's 2014 annual report says about 130 miles, which agrees within rounding. The Wayback copy of that report timed out in the verifier, but the live SEC page was read.

verifications.note: Trunkline's transmission system consists of one large diameter mainline pipeline with bi-directional capabilities, extending approximately 1,400 miles

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 3932.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 1400 mi. Energy Transfer's 2024 annual report puts the Trunkline mainline at about 1,400 miles. The sheet holds 3,932 km, which is 2,443 miles. Older reports show why: Panhandle's 2015 report also said 1,400 miles after about 680 miles were moved to crude oil service, and a Wikipedia article gives 3,059 miles for the whole system. The sheet figure does not match any current source.

The sheet held 3.40 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 2.1 mi. The federal notice says the project has 2.1 miles of new pipeline loop, about 3.4 km, the same as the sheet. EIA's August 2026 project list also gives 2.1 miles.

The sheet held 45.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 28 mi. The federal notice lists 28 miles of new 8-inch pipeline for the Columbia to Eastover project, about 45 km, the same as the sheet. EIA's list gives 29 miles, which is close.

verifications.note: approximately 7.7 miles of 42-inch pipeline looping facilities in Virginia
approximately 7.7 miles of 42-inch pipeline looping facilities in Virginia

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 12.90 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 7.7 mi. Two sources give the new loop as 7.7 miles, about 12.4 km. EIA's August 2026 list gives 7.72 miles. The sheet holds 12.9 km, which is 8.0 miles and matches none of them. The PDF text from the Williams release has stray spaces, so the verifier matched it but the phrase is spaced oddly in the file.

The sheet held 12070.08 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 7140 mi. Boardwalk's 2025 annual report lists Gulf South at 7,140 miles of pipeline as of December 31, 2025. The sheet holds 7,500 miles worth of km. Boardwalk's 2012 annual report listed 7,240 miles and the Gulf South web page says about 7,200 miles. No source found states 7,500, so the figure appears to be an older or rounded total.

The sheet held 651.80 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 405 mi. EIA's August 2026 workbook lists the Questar Southern Trails Pipeline conversion, completed in 2002, at 405 miles, 16 inches and 87 MMcf/d. That matches the sheet 651.8 km. Questar company text describes a 487-mile eastern branch and a 210-mile western branch, which is the whole original system and is a different scope. EIA's figure is the one that matches this row.

verifications.note: Project: DeRuyter Pipeline Replacement ... Length: 25 miles

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet held 40.20 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 25 mi. Pipeline and Gas Journal's October 2018 projects list shows NYSEG's DeRuyter Pipeline Replacement between Norwich and Oneonta, New York, at 25 miles and 10 inches. That matches the sheet 40.2 km. An earlier review found a news report quoting the utility's filing at about 50 miles of mains, so a person should choose between 25 and 50.

The sheet held 0.32 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 0.2 mi. The FERC assessment and the Federal Register notice both give 0.2 mile of interconnect piping in Cameron Parish. That matches the sheet 0.32 km. The notice says 20-inch and the assessment says 30-inch pipe, which is a diameter difference only.

The sheet held 35.41 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 20 mi. Pipeline and Gas Journal says the first phase of Hillabee had about 20 miles of looping. EIA's August 2026 workbook also lists Hillabee phase 1 at 20 miles. A search summary of a natural gas trade report gave 15.6 miles of 42-inch pipe plus 4.6 miles of 48-inch pipe, which adds to 20.2. The sheet 35.41 km equals 22 miles, so it is a little high.

The sheet held 129.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 80 mi. The 2020 federal environmental assessment calls the existing North Baja pipeline about 80 miles long. The sheet figure of 129 km is 80.2 miles, so it is a conversion of the 80 miles. Federal Register notices from 2000 and 2002 give 79.8 and 79.9 miles for the planned system. Those are earlier planning figures and are not proposed.

The sheet held 499.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 310 mi. Kinder Morgan states TransColorado as a 310-mile system. The sheet figure of 499 km is 310.1 miles, so it is a conversion of the 310 miles. The offshore-technology page gives the same length in km only, so it stays as it is.

The sheet held 370.10 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 230 mi. The Spectra Energy press release says the Renaissance pipeline runs 230 miles. The sheet figure of 370.1 km is 230 miles, so it is a conversion.

The sheet held 39.40 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 24.5 mi. The Pipeline and Gas Journal table lists Mountaineer Gas Pipeline Phase II, the Charlestown Loop, at 24.5 miles. The sheet figure of 39.4 km is 24.5 miles, so it is a conversion. A West Virginia Public Broadcasting story gives 29 miles for the second phase, which is a different and earlier plan and is not used.

The sheet held 423.30 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 263 mi. Two Securities and Exchange Commission filings state the MoGas pipeline as 263 miles. The sheet figure of 423.3 km is 263.0 miles, so it is a conversion. The 75-mile Omega system is separate and is not counted.

The sheet held 106.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 66 mi. Iroquois describes the NYMarc pipeline as about 66 miles long, 60 miles in New York and 6 in New Jersey. The sheet km figure is a conversion of the mile figure.

The sheet held 37.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 23 mi. The FERC notice describes a 23-mile pipeline from Texas Gas Transmission's line in Kentucky to Clarksville, Tennessee. The segments are 19.7 and 3.1 miles. The notice names Clarksville Gas and Water as the builder. The sheet km figure is a conversion of the mile figure.

The sheet held 60.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 37.1 mi. The newest EIA release lists the Northeast Supply Enhancement Project at 37.1 miles. That is about 59.7 km, so the sheet figure of 60 km is a conversion of it. The project scope includes a 23.5-mile offshore segment.

The sheet held 1585.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 985 mi. The 2014 news item gives the Bridgeline system as approximately 985 miles. The sheet value of 1585 km is a conversion of that figure. The page cited before no longer shows the figure, so an Oil and Gas Journal article is used. EnLink's current page says more than 1,000 miles.

The sheet held 1199.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 745 mi. The project profile states the total length as 745 miles with the km figure beside it. The sheet value of 1199 km is a conversion of the mile figure.

The sheet held 225.30 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 140 mi. The 2014 press release says the Prairie State Pipeline would be nearly 140 miles. The sheet value of 225.3 km is a conversion of 140 miles.

The sheet held 836.90 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 520 mi. The October 2018 planned projects table lists the Permian-Katy Pipeline at 520 miles, Waha to Katy. The sheet value of 836.9 km is a conversion of that figure.

The sheet held 33.80 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 21 mi. The 2019 environmental assessment gives the Stage 3 pipeline as about 21 miles. The sheet value of 33.8 km is a conversion of that figure.

The sheet held 9495.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 5900 mi. The Rextag page for Enable Gas Transmission gives the whole system as 5,900 miles. The sheet value of 9,495 km is that figure converted to kilometers.

The sheet held 595.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 370 mi. The 2010 Energy Transfer Partners annual report calls the East Texas pipeline a 370-mile natural gas pipeline. An archived Energy Transfer page from 2017 also says about 370 miles. The sheet value of 595 km is that figure converted to kilometers. Both pages call it the East Texas pipeline, not the East Texas Gas Pipeline.

The sheet held 669.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 416 mi. The TC PipeLines page for the Iroquois Gas Transmission System gives the length as 416 miles. The sheet value of 669 km is that figure converted to kilometers. The Iroquois company site says 414 miles, which is about 666 km, so 416 fits the sheet value better.

The sheet held 827.20 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 514 mi. The Fairbanks Pipeline Company technical page for the Arctic Fox pipeline gives both design cases as 514 miles from Prudhoe Bay to North Pole. The sheet value of 827.2 km is that figure converted to kilometers.

The sheet held 402.30 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 250 mi. The October 2018 Pipeline News list gives the Sooner Trails Pipeline Project as 250 miles, from Bryan County, Oklahoma to Lamar County, Texas. The sheet value of 402.3 km is that figure converted to kilometers. The EIA project table also says 250 miles but does not name it this way in the scan, so it was not relied on.

The sheet held 112.70 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 70 mi. The Tallgrass press release from June 2020 calls the Cheyenne Connector a 70-mile pipeline. The sheet value of 112.7 km is that figure converted to kilometers. One news site gives 113 km, which is the same length in kilometers.

The sheet held 2574.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 1600 mi. The Enable Midstream page says Mississippi River Transmission has about 1,600 miles of pipeline. The sheet value of 2,574 km is that figure converted.

The sheet held 692.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 430 mi. The EIA workbook lists Permian Highway Pipeline Project at 430 miles. The 2026 EIA workbook also lists it at 430 miles in its historical sheet. The sheet 692 km is that figure converted. An Oil and Gas Journal article is used in place of an older EIA release.

The sheet held 24.10 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 15 mi. The Pipeline and Gas Journal table lists the Montour Lateral at 15 miles. A Talen Energy press release from June 2016 also describes a 15 mile lateral to the Montour plant but does not use the lateral's full name. The sheet 24.1 km is 15 miles converted.

The sheet held 10.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 10 mi. The table says 10 miles. The sheet has the number 10 with units km, so this is not a conversion. The number was already the mile figure and only the unit label is wrong. Staging 10 mi would make the km column read about 16.1. A person should confirm that before it is applied. The number was right but the unit was wrong.

The sheet held 35.40 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 22 mi. The newest EIA workbook lists the Index 99 Expansion Project of Gulf South Pipeline at 22 miles. The sheet 35.4 km is that figure converted.

The sheet held 1817.00 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 1129 mi. The operator's page says 1,129 miles. The sheet km figure is that mileage converted. A pipeline safety brochure from Kansas gives 1,120 miles, which is a slightly older figure. The live page now returns not found, so its archived copy is cited.

The sheet held 43.50 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 27 mi. The public radio story says the cancelled line would have run about 27 miles. The sheet km figure is that mileage converted. The other current ref could not be opened.

The sheet held 48.30 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 30 mi. The 2018 planned projects list says 30 miles. The sheet km figure is that mileage converted. The 2014 federal environmental review notice gives 29.8 miles, which is close.

The sheet held 80.50 km. The source states the length in miles, so it goes back to 50 mi. The 2020 federal pipeline safety letter calls Line 1600 a 50-mile line. The sheet km figure is that mileage converted. A 2018 state utility commission response gives 49.7 miles.
